cards.explanation: The message says to be careful not to pass by that place. Elisha, the man of God, sends word to the king of Israel: "Be careful not to pass by this place, for the Arameans are going down there." (2 Kings 6:9) It's a warning, plain and simple. Aram picks the spot and Elisha tells Israel to steer clear of it.

The answer is False. The king doesn't ignore the warning. He sends word to the place the man of God pointed out. (2 Kings 6:10) Elisha warns him time and again, and the king stays on his guard in those places. I think that's a king who is paying attention.

The king of Aram thinks it's someone on his own side. He is enraged and asks his servants, "Tell me, which one of us is on the side of the king of Israel?" (2 Kings 6:11) He thinks the leak is somebody in his own camp. It's like the cookies keep vanishing and you start side-eyeing the whole kitchen.

The answer is bedroom. The servant says Elisha tells the king of Israel "…the very words you speak in your bedroom." (2 Kings 6:12) A bedroom is the one room where you figure nobody's listening. Elisha, the prophet in Israel, somehow knows it all anyway.
The answer is Dothan. The report comes in: "Elisha is in Dothan…" (2 Kings 6:13) The king of Aram wanted to know where Elisha was so he could send men to capture him. Now he has a spot on the map.
The answer is army. The king of Aram sends "…horses, chariots, and a great army." (2 Kings 6:14) That's a lot of force headed for one man of God. I think that king wasn't taking any chances.

The answer is True. The servant sees the army and says, "Oh, my master, what are we to do?" (2 Kings 6:15) He gets up early, steps outside, and there they are, horses and chariots all around the city. I think I'd be asking the same question.

The reason Elisha gives is that there are more with us than with them. He says, "Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them." (2 Kings 6:16) The army outside is easy to see, and Elisha is pointing to something that isn't. His reason is about who is with Elisha and his servant.

The answer is Elisha. The LORD opens the young man's eyes, and he sees that "…the hills were full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha." (2 Kings 6:17) Earlier he had seen an army with horses and chariots surrounding the city. (2 Kings 6:15) Now he sees what Elisha meant.

Elisha asks the LORD to strike them with blindness. He prays, "Please strike these people with blindness." (2 Kings 6:18) The Arameans are coming down against him, and that's his request. Then the text says, "So He struck them with blindness, according to the word of Elisha."

The answer is True. Elisha tells them, "This is not the way, and this is not the city." (2 Kings 6:19) He says it after the LORD struck them with blindness. (2 Kings 6:18) Then he tells them to follow him and says he will take them to the man they are seeking.

The answer is Samaria. The text says, "And he led them to Samaria." (2 Kings 6:19) Elisha had told them, "Follow me…" The Arameans were blind the whole walk. Then once they entered Samaria, the LORD opened their eyes. (2 Kings 6:20)
The answer is eyes. Elisha prays, "O LORD, open the eyes of these men that they may see." (2 Kings 6:20) Then the LORD opens their eyes. They look around and discover they're in Samaria.

The king of Israel asks Elisha whether he should kill them. He says, "My father, shall I kill them? Shall I kill them?" (2 Kings 6:21) He asks Elisha before he does anything. I think that says something about who he trusts to give the answer.
The answer is False. Elisha says, "Do not kill them…" (2 Kings 6:22) Then he asks the king whether he would kill those he had captured with his own sword or bow. Elisha's answer to the king is no.

Elisha tells the king to set food and water before them. He says, "Set food and water before them, that they may eat and drink and then return to their master." (2 Kings 6:22) These men came to capture him. Now they're getting a meal.

The answer is feast. The text says, "So the king prepared a great feast for them…" (2 Kings 6:23) Elisha only said to set out food and water, and the king goes big. After they finish eating and drinking, he sends them away.

The answer is True. The passage ends, "And the Aramean raiders did not come into the land of Israel again." (2 Kings 6:23) Before that, the king prepared a great feast for them and sent them away, and they returned to their master. Then the raiders stop coming.
